courseDescription: Learn Java programming from scratch - perfect for beginners!

lessons.title: Introduction to Java
lessons.description: Learn about Java, its history, and how to write your first program
objectives: Understand what Java is and why it's popular
Write and run your first Java program

content.content: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language developed by Sun Microsystems in 1995. It follows the principle of 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' (WORA), meaning compiled Java code can run on any platform that supports Java without recompilation.

Java is widely used for:
• Web applications (backend)
• Android mobile apps
• Enterprise software
• Scientific computing
• Big data technologies

content.explanation: This is your first Java program! The 'public class HelloWorld' defines a class named HelloWorld. The 'main' method is the entry point where the program starts. System.out.println prints text to the console.

content.title: Understanding Program Structure
content.description: Every Java program must have a class and a main method to run

lessons.summary: Java is a powerful, platform-independent programming language. Every Java program needs a class with a main method to execute.
keyPoints: Java is platform-independent (WORA)
Every Java program needs a class
The main method is the entry point
System.out.println() prints output
Java files have .java extension

practiceExercise.task: Write a Java program that prints your name and age on separate lines
practiceExercise.hint: Use System.out.println() twice - once for name, once for age

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.description: Learn how to store and manipulate data using variables
objectives: Understand different data types in Java

content.content: Variables are containers for storing data values. In Java, each variable must have a specific data type that determines what kind of data it can hold.

content.code:
// Primitive Data Types
byte b = 100;          // 8-bit integer
short s = 1000;        // 16-bit integer
int age = 25;          // 32-bit integer (most common)
long big = 100000L;    // 64-bit integer
float price = 19.99f;  // 32-bit decimal
double pi = 3.14159;   // 64-bit decimal (most common)
char grade = 'A';      // Single character
boolean isJavaFun = true; // true or false
content.explanation: Java has 8 primitive data types. int and double are the most commonly used. Notice the 'f' suffix for float and 'L' for long.

content.title: Working with Variables
content.description: Declare variables, assign values, and perform operations

lessons.summary: Variables store data in Java. Each variable has a type that determines what data it can hold. Use descriptive names for variables.
keyPoints: Variables must be declared with a type
Java has 8 primitive data types
String is a reference type (not primitive)
Use camelCase for variable names
Variables can be updated after declaration

practiceExercise.task: Create variables for your name (String), age (int), height (double), and whether you like programming (boolean). Print all of them.
practiceExercise.hint: String uses double quotes, char uses single quotes

lessons.title: Control Flow - If/Else
lessons.description: Learn how to make decisions in your code using conditional statements
objectives: Use if, else if, and else statements

content.content: Control flow statements allow your program to make decisions and execute different code based on conditions. The if-else statement is the most basic form of control flow.

content.explanation: The if statement checks conditions from top to bottom. The first condition that is true executes its block. If none are true, the else block runs.

content.title: Number Checker
content.description: Check if a number is positive, negative, or zero

lessons.summary: If-else statements let your code make decisions. Use comparison operators (>, <, ==, !=, >=, <=) to create conditions.
keyPoints: if executes code when condition is true
else if checks additional conditions
else runs when no conditions are true
Use == to compare values (not =)
Conditions must be boolean expressions

practiceExercise.task: Write a program that takes a temperature (int) and prints: 'Hot' if > 30, 'Warm' if > 20, 'Cool' if > 10, 'Cold' otherwise
practiceExercise.hint: Check the highest temperature first, then work down

lessons.title: Loops - For and While
lessons.description: Learn how to repeat actions using loops
objectives: Use for loops for counted repetition
Use while loops for conditional repetition

content.content: Loops allow you to execute a block of code multiple times. Java has three types of loops: for, while, and do-while. Each is useful in different situations.

content.explanation: For loops have initialization, condition, and increment in one line. While loops only have a condition and are useful when the number of iterations is unknown.

content.title: Multiplication Table
content.description: Print the multiplication table for any number

lessons.summary: Loops repeat code. Use for loops when you know the count, while loops when you have a condition to check.
keyPoints: For loop: for(init; condition; increment)
While loop: while(condition)
Be careful of infinite loops
Use break to exit a loop early
Use continue to skip to next iteration

practiceExercise.task: Write a program that counts down from 10 to 1, then prints 'Blastoff!'
practiceExercise.hint: Start at 10, go down while > 0, decrement by 1 each time

lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.description: Learn how to store and manage multiple values using arrays
objectives: Understand what arrays are and why they're useful

content.content: An array is a container object that holds a fixed number of values of a single type. Arrays are useful when you need to work with multiple related values.

content.explanation: Arrays use zero-based indexing (first element is at index 0). The length property tells you how many elements are in the array.

content.title: Find Maximum in Array
content.description: Find the largest number in an array

lessons.summary: Arrays store multiple values of the same type. Use indexes to access elements, and loops to process all elements.
keyPoints: Arrays have fixed size (cannot change after creation)
Index starts at 0, ends at length-1
Use .length to get array size
All elements must be the same type
Use loops to process array elements

practiceExercise.task: Create an array of 5 test scores. Calculate and print the average score.
practiceExercise.hint: Add all scores together, then divide by the number of scores
